patch_description: The recommendation suggests combining insertion moves (best performing, 277.00) with pairwise-swap moves (296.00) in a hybrid neighborhood. Adjacent-swap-only local search can get stuck: an insertion move relocates a transaction to any position (not just ±1), unlocking improvements swaps cannot reach, while swaps reorder without removing/reinserting. I replace the adjacent-swap-only local search with a hybrid that does a full best-insertion sweep followed by a full adjacent-swap sweep each pass, iterating until no improvement. This dominates the previous neighborhood (adjacent swaps are a subset of insertion+swap reach) at modest extra cost, since each candidate move is evaluated with the true makespan via `get_opt_seq_cost`.
